title: Procedure call entry
statement: Let $S$ be a compiler setting, and suppose a call statement with procedure index $p$, argument expressions $args$, and return-variable index $x$ starts at depth $d$, code position $pos$, stack base $q$, state $σ$, and word memory $m$. Assume the starting conditions hold, every argument expression is safe in $σ$, $d$ is less than the depth limit, and procedure $p$ has entry position $e$. Then there is a word memory $m_2$ such that the compiled machine takes exactly the call-size number of steps from $(pos,m)$ to position $e$ with memory $m_2$. This memory represents the callee state whose local frame consists of the argument values and whose ordinary memory is inherited from $σ$; its stack cell at index $q+F$ contains the return position $pos$ plus the call size; and it agrees with $m$ outside the cells writable from stack base $q+F$.
hypotheses_covered: all argument expressions are safe in the initial state
call depth is strictly below the depth limit
procedure entry list gives procedure $p$ the position $e$
replaced:
Let $S$ be a compiler setting, $d$ a call depth, $p$ a procedure index, $args$ a list of
argument expressions, $x$ a return-variable index, $σ$ a state, and $pos,q,m$ an initial
code position, stack base, and memory. Suppose the starting conditions hold for this
call, every argument expression is safe in $σ$, $d$ is less than the depth limit, and
the entry position for procedure $p$ is $e$. Then there is a memory $m_2$ such that the
machine takes exactly the call-size number of steps from position $pos$ and memory $m$
to position $e$ and memory $m_2$; $m_2$ represents the callee state with argument values
as its local frame and the original memory contents; the stack cell at index $q+F$
stores the return position $pos+callSize(F,args)$; and $m_2$ agrees with $m$ outside the
cells writable from stack base $q+F$.
